title: Writing validation and authentication
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Validation and authentication
objectives: know how to code a presence, type, range, length and format check
understand how a validation loop keeps asking until the value typed in passes every check
know how to code an authentication check that allows only a set number of attempts
starter: A program reads an age with age = int(input()) and the user types the word twelve. Write down what happens to the program, and the check that should have come before the cast.

stations.name: Checking the input
stations.fact: Validation checks data is sensible, not that it is true: a wrong but sensible date passes every check.
stations.challenge: Why must a type check happen before the value is cast?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a word. Take off any spaces at each end of it. Display nothing typed when nothing is left. Otherwise display value [the word without those spaces].
Ask the user for a whole number. Check whether every character typed is a digit. Display number: [the number] when they are all digits. Display not a number instead when any one of them is not.
Ask the user for a word. Check it against red, green and blue, which are fixed in the program. Display known when it is one of those three. Display unknown instead when it is not.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Range checks
stations.fact: Negative values are fine for a temperature but never for an age, so a range check must suit its data.
stations.challenge: Which two values would you test on a score that must be 1 to 10?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a whole number. Display valid when it is from 1 to 10 inclusive. Display too low instead when it is below 1. Display too high instead when it is above 10.
Ask the user for a whole number. Display not a number when what was typed is not a whole number. Display ok when it is from -5 to 35 inclusive. Display out of range when it is outside that range.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Length and format checks
stations.fact: isalpha(), isdigit() and isnumeric() each answer one format question about a whole string at once.
stations.challenge: Describe the checks a reference of two letters then four digits needs.

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a word. Display too short when it is under 8 characters. Display too long when it is over 16 characters. Display ok for anything in between.
Ask the user for a code. Take off any spaces at each end of it. Display valid code when it is two letters and then four digits. Display invalid code instead when it is not.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Keeping asking
stations.fact: A loop that keeps asking until the data is right is the simplest defensive design there is.
stations.challenge: Why should a program say what was wrong rather than just 'invalid'?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Keep asking the user for a word until one still has something in it once the spaces at each end have been taken off. Display that is empty for every wrong one. Then display accepted [the word without those spaces] for the one you take.
Keep asking the user for a whole number until one is from 1 to 5 inclusive. Display please enter 1 to 5 for every wrong one. Then display chosen [the number] for the one you accept.

Keep asking the user for a whole number until one is from 10 to 99 inclusive. Display that is not a whole number when what was typed is not all digits. Display that is outside 10 to 99 when it is a number outside that range. Then display accepted: [the number] for the one you accept.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Authentication
stations.fact: Validation checks data and authentication checks people, and the exam asks for that difference often.
stations.challenge: What is the difference between validation and authentication?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a line of usernames. Then ask for a line of passwords in the same order. Then ask for one username to check. Then ask for one password to check. Display unknown user when the username is not listed. Display wrong password when the password does not match. Display access granted when both match.

Ask the user for the correct passcode. Then ask for one attempt at a time. Display wrong passcode for each miss. Display access granted as soon as one matches. Then display account locked if a third attempt has missed too.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Putting it together
stations.fact: Skipping a bad line and counting it is often better than stopping: the report still comes out.
stations.challenge: Plan the checks a club sign-up needs for a username and an age.

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Keep asking the user for a username until one is 5 to 12 characters of letters and digits only. Then keep asking for a whole number until one is from 11 to 19 inclusive. Display registered [the username] [the number] at the end.

Keep asking the user for word,number lines until one is exactly done. Display added [the word] for each good line. Then display accepted: [how many were added] on the next line. Then display total: [their numbers added up] on the last line.

final.title: Final challenge: which check?
final.instr: write your answer for each one.
rows: The field has not been left empty
Something was typed before Enter
The value is a whole number
The reading is a number, not a word
The score is from 1 to 10
The password is 8 to 16 characters
The reference is two letters then four digits
The date is written as DD/MM/YYYY

keyq: Why is refusing bad data better than letting a program stop with an error?
exam: A range check for a satisfaction score that must be from 1 to 10 inclusive is written if score > 1 and score < 10. State the two scores this wrongly refuses, and write the condition corrected.
Write a program that keeps asking for a tutor group code of exactly one letter followed by two digits until a valid one is typed.
Write a program that allows three attempts at the four-digit passcode 2471, and prints Locked if all three attempts are wrong.
